summary: The narrator slips during descent, then rolls and arrests the fall by catching a tree. The Turoyo sequence supports ordinary slipping within inherited sense 1, not a specialised skiing event.
šayənno is consistent with first-person n following a stem-final r and the resulting nn sequence. This single occurrence does not establish a broader dialectal distribution.

The same 93/50 Turoyo is already quoted in the entry with an inherited English translation. Retain that existing text; there is no new example for which a translated replacement should be manufactured.
No evidence here bears on the inherited Ski laufen component or the unrelated advising homonym šyr 2.
kšurena and šuranwo are respectively current/habitual and past repeated pursuit in one report, with human subjects and bəṯr targets. They are separate tokens, not independent corroborating texts.

Neither verse contains slipping, loss of footing, skiing or another diagnostic link to šyr 1. Root affiliation remains undetermined, so there is no publishable extension to pursuit or new form for this root.
Lookup šwr gives II advising, not this simple pursuit paradigm. Form lookup šur returns several weak-root candidates; consonant matching does not resolve the attribution.

Round 1 provides secure slipping evidence already represented in the base entry. It offers no basis for changing that sense here. The Jan English is project machine translation and is not used to resolve the uncertain root.
Identify the lexeme and base forms of kšurena / šuranwo at Jan 2.22/4017. Does it mean chase, run after, slide, or something else? Until identified, the proposed šyr 1 bəṯr construction is withheld.
